name: SAGE

facility_roles.note: Sourced from Wikipedia (rank 12) only this session.

intervals.label: commissioning (gallium extractions, background reduction)
intervals.quote: Extractions on approximately 30 tons of Ga began in 1988; by late 1989 backgrounds were low enough to begin solar neutrino measurements.
intervals.note: Start is the year extractions began on about 30 tons of gallium (SAGE 1999 paper, arXiv:astro-ph/9907113); end is the December 1989 start of solar-neutrino measurements stated in the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200). Replaces an earlier Wikipedia-infobox 'construction / start' row (1989-12 to 1990-01) that the collaboration papers do not support as a construction period.

intervals.label: primary data-taking
intervals.quote: For all SAGE data from January 1990 through December 2007 (168 runs and 310 separate counting sets)
intervals.note: December 2007 is the end of the dataset analysed in the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200), not a stop of data-taking; the next row records that measurements continued.

intervals.label: continued operations
intervals.quote: Measurements have continued with only a few brief interruptions since that time.
intervals.note: The SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200) says measurements have continued since December 1989. Wikipedia says the data run through August 2011 and that the experiment was ongoing in 2016-2017, but no authoritative source fetched here confirms the status after 2009. Left open (`end: null`, ongoing at `verified_at` per §2.3) rather than asserting either a firm shutdown or firm continuation.

physics_goals.value: Measure the flux of low-energy (pp-chain) solar neutrinos via the radiochemical gallium-to-germanium reaction
physics_goals.quote: to measure the flux of solar neutrinos
physics_goals.note: Sourced from Wikipedia (rank 12) only this session.

unique_capabilities.value: Radiochemical liquid-gallium target sensitive to the lowest-energy (pp) solar neutrinos
unique_capabilities.quote: In contrast to all other present or past solar neutrino experiments, the radiochemical Ga experiment, because of its low threshold of 233 keV, is sensitive to all components of the
unique_capabilities.note: Quote states sensitivity to all components of the solar neutrino flux (including pp) because of the 233 keV threshold; 'lowest-energy (pp)' in the value is the reading that follows from that.

quantity.quote: The mass of gallium used in SAGE at the present time is 50 tonnes.
quantity.note: 50 t is the mass stated in the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200). The target mass varied over time: the 1999 SAGE paper (arXiv:astro-ph/9907113) says the extraction mass was increased to nearly 60 tons in summer 1991, and Wikipedia gives a range of 50-57 tonnes.

summary.plain: An experiment deep inside a Russian mountain that uses tonnes of liquid gallium metal to catch the Sun's lowest-energy neutrinos.
summary.technical: Radiochemical liquid-gallium solar-neutrino experiment at the Baksan Neutrino Observatory, Russia, under a rock overburden equivalent to 4700 m of water; 50 t gallium target. Measured a solar neutrino capture rate of 67.2 (+7.2/-7.0 stat) (+3.5/-3.0 syst) SNU over 1990-1997, about half the Standard Solar Model prediction of 129 SNU.
